candidates.tagline: The self-driving car that's supposed to be better than humans can't get through a construction zone.
candidates.story: On November 11, 2026, California's DMV banned Waymo's autonomous robotaxis from all state freeways after three vehicles drove into an active construction closure on US Route 101 near Burlingame — a hazard human drivers handle by simply slowing down and reading signs. This came after the same thing happened in May 2026, Waymo pushed a software fix in July, resumed freeway service, then drove into construction zones again. The DMV called the repeated incursions an 'imminent hazard to public safety.' Waymo responded by suspending freeway operations in all its markets nationwide.
candidates.why_funny: Waymo's entire sales pitch is 'we're safer than human drivers' — and human drivers handle construction zones just by seeing the orange cones and slowing down; Waymo needed two failures, one fix, one recall, and a nationwide suspension to still not solve it.
candidates.alt: White Waymo Jaguar I-PACE autonomous robotaxi with its distinctive black sensor dome on the roof, driving on a residential street in Austin, Texas — the same model repeatedly drove into active highway construction zones in California, triggering a statewide freeway ban by the DMV

candidates.tagline: Samsung spent months mocking Apple's phone. Its next flagship will look just like Apple's phone.
candidates.story: Leaked CAD renders of the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra, confirmed by multiple independent tipsters in November 2026, show the flagship abandoning its distinctive vertical camera stack for a wide horizontal camera plateau nearly identical to the iPhone 17 and 18 Pro — while Samsung has simultaneously been running global billboard and social media campaigns mocking Apple's cracking iPhone Duo foldable. Tom's Guide warned the redesign could cause 'the most intense wave of criticism in Galaxy history,' and ProPakistani headlined it 'Samsung to Copy iPhone Design After Months of Mocking Apple.'
candidates.why_funny: Samsung has built its entire brand identity around 'we're not Apple' and runs ongoing global ads mocking Apple — while designing its next flagship to look exactly like Apple.
candidates.alt: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra in dark violet shown from the back at a Samsung retail store in Japan, displaying its distinctive vertical four-lens camera arrangement — the design Samsung's next S27 Ultra will reportedly replace with a wide horizontal camera plateau nearly identical to Apple's iPhone 17 Pro
